instructions: Mince the 2 garlic cloves and finely chop 3 tbsp of the onion. Chop 1/4 cup of the basil and grate 1/3 cup of the Romano.
In a large bowl, whisk the egg with the chopped basil, the 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp pepper, 1/2 tsp oregano, the garlic and 2 tbsp water.
Add the onion, the 1.25 lb turkey, the 2/3 cup breadcrumbs and the grated Romano. Mix it with your hands until it looks even all the way through and stop there.
Wet your hands with water and roll the mixture into balls a little bigger than a golf ball. Wet your hands again whenever it starts to stick. You should get about 18.

Heat the 2 tbsp olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat until it shimmers. Add the meatballs in a single layer with a little space between them. Let them brown for about 2 minutes before you turn them, and keep turning them until they're browned on all sides, 7 to 8 minutes in all.

Pour the jar of marinara over the meatballs and bring it to a boil. Turn the heat to low, cover the pan tightly and simmer for 15 minutes. You're cooking them to 165°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one there. No thermometer? Cut one open: it's done when there's no pink left in the center.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Tear a few basil leaves over the top and grate on some more Romano.

Serve over spaghetti or with crusty bread. If you'd like some for a busy night, let the extra meatballs and sauce cool, then freeze them in a container for up to 3 months. Thaw them in the fridge overnight and warm them, covered, over low heat.
method_notes: All three bind about a pound of 93% lean turkey with an egg, breadcrumbs, grated cheese, garlic, oregano and fresh herbs, and keep the mixing light so the meatballs stay tender. Once Upon a Chef adds a little water and minced onion, browns the meatballs in a skillet and simmers them covered in a jar of marinara for 15 minutes to 165°F. Well Plated bakes them at 375°F for 15 minutes and spoons warmed sauce over the top, and Cooking Classy soaks the crumbs in milk, bakes at 450°F and tosses the meatballs in marinara at the end. This follows Once Upon a Chef, written with the 1.25 lb package turkey comes in.
